questions.question:
**The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.**

Would you / like to / watch an movie / tonight at eight?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: "**watch an movie**".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The correct phrase is "**watch a movie**" instead of "**watch an movie**".
 
• The article "**an**" is used before a word that starts with a vowel sound, while the word "**movie**" starts with a consonant sound.
 
• The correct sentence should be "*Would you like to watch a movie tonight at eight?*"

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 1**.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.**

Teja is a successful businessman; he always __makes hay when the moon shines__.

options.text: makes hay while the sun sets
makes hay while the sun shines
makes hey while the moon rises
makes hay while the stars twinkle

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: "**makes hay while the sun shines**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original phrase "**he always makes hay when the moon shines**" is a play on the traditional idiom "**make hay while the sun shines**."
 
• The original idiom means to take advantage of favourable conditions or opportunities. (अनुकूल परिस्थितियों या अवसरों का लाभ उठाना)
 
 
• **Example**: *Recognizing the potential for growth, Alex decided to make hay while the sun shines__ and invested in the booming tech industry.*
 
 
 
• In the context of Teja being a successful businessman, it suggests that he seizes opportunities when they arise.
 
• The suggested substitution, "**he always makes hay when the sun shines**," adheres more closely to the conventional idiom.
 
• The phrase "**when the sun shines**" reinforces the idea of utilizing favourable conditions for one's benefit.

Thus, **option 2** is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.**

Did the company launch a new product last month?

options.text: Did the new product launch the company last month?
Was the company launched by a new product last month?
Was a new product launched by the company last month?
Did the new product launch by the company last month's?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: "**Was a new product launched by the company last month?**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• To convert an active sentence into a passive voice, the object of the active sentence becomes the subject of the passive sentence.
 
• The verb is changed to its past participle form and "**by**" is used to introduce the doer of the action in the passive sentence.
 
• In this case, "**the company**" is the object of the active sentence, so it becomes the subject of the passive sentence.
 
• "**Launch**" becomes "**launched**" in its past participle form.
 
• The sentence in passive voice becomes "*Was a new product launched by the company last month?*"

Thus, **option 3** is the correct answer

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined words in the following sentence.**

I am trying to study, __if it is impossible__ with all this noise.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: "**but it is impossible**."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original sentence expresses a contrast between the speaker's desire to study and the distracting noise.
 
• '**But**' expresses this contrast and maintains the original meaning.
 
• The conjunction "**but**" is used to indicate a contrast or contradiction between the two clauses.
 
• In this case, the first part of the sentence expresses the effort to study, and the second part introduces the obstacle (noise) that makes studying impossible.
 
• Using "**but**" clarifies the relationship between these contrasting elements, resulting in a more coherent and grammatically correct sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 2**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• '**If**': Used to introduce a condition or a possibility.
 
• '**That**': Often used to introduce a clause, provide additional information, or indicate a consequence.
 
• '**While**': Used to indicate a contrast or simultaneous occurrence.
 
• '**Unless**': Indicates a condition that must be met for a certain outcome to happen.

Having an irritated and unfriendly attitude

questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The idiom "**having a chip on one's shoulder**" means to be easily offended or to have a confrontational attitude. (आसानी से नाराज हो जाना या टकरावपूर्ण रवैया अपनाना)
 
• This idiom comes from the practice of placing a chip of wood on one's shoulder and daring others to knock it off as a sign of readiness for a fight.
 
• Someone with a chip on their shoulder may feel that they have been wronged or unfairly treated in the past, leading to their defensive or hostile behaviour.
 
 
• **Examples**:
 
 
• *Ever since he got passed over for that promotion, he's had a real chip on his shoulder.*
 
• *Don't take it personally - she just has a chip on her shoulder about everything.*
 
 
 
 

Therefore, **option 2** is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Select the option that arranges the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.**

A) he has been

B) everyone he knows

C) so upset about his

D) him so rude to

E) divorce and that made
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **A, C, E, D, B.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **A- "He has been"**: This part sets the subject and introduces a state or condition.
 
• **C- "So upset about his"**: This part provides more information about the subject's emotional state, giving context to the upcoming events.
 
• **E- "Divorce and that made"**: This part introduces the reason for the subject's emotional state, explaining what caused him to be upset.
 
• **D- "Him so rude to"**: This part describes a consequence of the emotional state mentioned earlier, indicating the effect of his upset feelings.
 
• **B- "Everyone he knows"**: This part concludes the sentence by specifying the scope of the impact, indicating that his emotional state has affected those around him.
 
• So, when arranged in the sequence **A, C, E, D, B** the parts form a coherent and meaningful sentence with a clear flow of events and information.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 3**.

questions.question:
**Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.**

A. what to tell you and how to say it

B. and there is darkness everywhere

C. and I do not quite know

D. the light has gone out of our lives
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **DBCA**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Part D**: This part sets the sombre tone of the sentence, conveying a sense of loss or despair.
 
• **Part B**: This part builds upon the previous statement, emphasizing the bleakness of the situation by using the metaphor of darkness.
 
• **Part C**: This part introduces a personal reflection, expressing uncertainty or a lack of understanding about the current circumstances.
 
• **Part A**: This part concludes the sentence by expressing difficulty in finding the right words or conveying the emotions associated with the loss. It provides insight into the speaker's struggle to communicate the depth of their feelings.
 
• So, when arranged in the sequence **DBCA**, the parts form a coherent and meaningful sentence, capturing a sense of sorrow, uncertainty, and difficulty in articulating emotions.

Therefore, **option 2** is the correct answer.
